The spelling bee winners were announced and given certificates. A paraprofessional was awarded and given recognition for her work with children with autism. They announced their tentative budget that could cause a 6.69% tax increase. Council Member Wojtowicz- The Wildcat Ridge Preserve, a 123-acre wooded tract in Rockaway Township, has officially been preserved as open space following a sale closing on a project funded through a $1.04 million grant from the Morris County Open Space Preservation Trust Fund. The grant, approved by the Morris County Board of County Commissioners, enabled The Land Conservancy of New Jersey to secure the property. The closing on March 12, 2026, represents the first finalization of purchases involving three open space grants approved in November, authorizing nearly $7 million to preserve 192.3 acres across three municipalities. Council Member Kelley - On March 11th, I attended the Water Department building name dedication/celebration. On March 16th, I visited the areas of power loss, due to extremely high winds, in the Meriden and Valley Road sections of the 6th Ward. During my visit, I spoke with NG Gilbert and Verizon regarding power and communication restoration time frames. I Followed up with Police Chief Scheer regarding recorded data and speeding concerns on Decker/Lyonsville Road [still waiting for the recorded data]. I prepared for and participated in the March 14, 2026 public budget meeting. It was great to see many members of the public that attended. During the budget meeting I made many motions to cut over $300,000 of fat within the budget, increase revenues and public safety. However, the majority of council members were not interested in those areas of reductions to save taxpayer's money. 12. ADJOURNMENT: * NEXT TOWNSHIP COUNCIL REGULARY MEETING – APRIL 14TH*

GOVERNING BOARD AGENDA REGULAR MEETING – Board Actions Tuesday, July 14, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. Duffy Community Center Multipurpose Room 5145 E. Fifth Street Tucson, AZ 85711 1. SCHEDULED EXECUTIVE MEETING - 4:30 p.m. 1.1 Roll Call 4:31 p.m. Board Member attendance was established via roll call. Those in attendance were Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah. Val Romero and Sadie Shaw were not present for roll call. 1.2 Motion to Convene Executive Meeting 4:31 p.m. Motion to go into executive meeting at this time to consider one or more of the following matters: Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah Not present: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw Motion Passed 3-0 1.3 Personnel Matters 1.4 Negotiations for the Purchase, Sale, or Lease of Real Property 1.5 Negotiations with Employee Groups 1.6 Adjourn Executive Meeting and Reconvene Regular Meeting 2. RECONVENE REGULAR MEETING – CALL TO ORDER – 5:30 p.m. 2.1 Roll Call 5:46 p.m. Board Member attendance was established via roll call. Those in attendance were Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah. 2.2 Land Acknowledgement Statement 5:47 p.m. Isabella Patterson Maldonado, 12th grader at Catalina High School, read the Land Acknowledgement Statement.
2.3 Pledge of Allegiance 5:48 p.m. Pledge led by Isabella Patterson Maldonado, 12th grader at Catalina High School. 2.4 Agenda Adjustments 5:48 p.m. Dr. Trujillo recommended moving item 9.2 to after Call to the Audience. By unanimous consent to move item 9.2 to after Call to the Audience. 3. SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT 3.1 Superintendent's Report 5:49 p.m. Details are available via the video and audio recordings on the TUSD website at https://tusd1-schooldesk.community.highbond.com/Portal/ . Dr. Trujillo spoke In Memoriam of Patty Lopez, TUSD Educator. The board held a moment of silence at 5:58 p.m. 4. CALL TO THE AUDIENCE 4.1 Guidelines to Address the Board 5:58 p.m. 6:05 p.m. Point of order by Sadie Shaw due to technical issues. 6:11 p.m. Recess meeting due to technical issues. 6:21 p.m. Reconvene meeting. Ravi Shah closed the Call to the Audience at 6:35 p.m. 5. CONSENT AGENDA (All items listed will be considered as a group with one motion. There will not be separate discussion of these items unless a Board Member so requests, in which case the item will be removed from the consent agenda and considered as a separate item.) 5.1 Approval of Consent Agenda Items 5.2 through 5.19 6:37 p.m. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0
5.2 Approval of Talent Acquisition, Transfers, Separations, Changes, Payouts, and Leaves of Absence Motion to approve the Talent Acquisition personnel lists. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.3 Approval of Consortium Agreement between Tucson Unified School District, the Sunnyside Unified School District, and the Arizona Board of Regents from the University of Arizona Psychology Internship Consortium Motion to approve Consortium Agreement between Tucson Unified School District, the Sunnyside Unified School District, and the Arizona Board of Regents from the University of Arizona Psychology Internship Consortium, as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.4 Approval of the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District and the Arizona Department of Economic Security/Rehabilitation Services Administration for the Transition from School to Work (TSW) Program Motion to approve the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District and the Arizona Department of Economic Security/Rehabilitation Services Administration for the Transition from School to Work (TSW) Program, as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.5 Approval of Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District and the Arizona Board of Regents, University of Arizona College of Education Project FOCUS: Enhanced Academic and Transition Services for High School Students with Disabilities
Motion to approve the Intergovernmental Agreement between Tucson Unified School District and the Arizona Board of Regents, University of Arizona College of Education Project FOCUS: Enhanced Academic and Transition Services for High School Students with Disabilities, as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.6 Approval of Amendment I to the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) with Tucson Unified School District and Pima County Community & Workforce Development Department for the Pima Early Education Program (PEEPS) Motion to approve Amendment I to the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) with Tucson Unified School District and Pima County Community & Workforce Development Department for the Pima Early Education Program (PEEPS). Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.7 Approval of the Lease Agreement with Premium Parking at Tucson High Magnet School, with Authorization for the Operations Program Manager to Execute the Agreement Motion to approve the Lease Agreement with Premium Parking at Tucson High Magnet School, with Authorization for the Operations Program Manager to Execute the Agreement. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.8 Approval of Pima JTED Project SEARCH: Enhanced Academic and Transition Services for High School Students with Disabilities
Motion to approve Pima JTED Project SEARCH: Enhanced Academic and Transition Services for High School Students with Disabilities. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.9 Approval to Award Request for Proposal (RFP) 27-017-TUSD1 – Temporary Staffing Services, as needed 6:37 p.m. Motion to approve Request for Proposal (RFP) 27-017-TUSD1 – Temporary Staffing Services, as needed. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.10 Correction of 4% Override Rate Increase for Substitute Teachers Motion to approve the corrected daily rates, which includes the 4% increase, for substitute teachers and funded with the Maintenance & Operations Override. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.11 Reauthorization of Change Funds for the 2026-27 Fiscal Year Motion to approve the reauthorization of District Change Funds for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0
5.12 Reauthorization of Tucson Unified School District Bank Accounts & Authorized Signers for the 2026-27 Fiscal Year Motion to approve reauthorization of Tucson Unified School District bank accounts & authorized signers for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.13 Approval of the Revised Extracurricular Activities Fees Schedule for the 2026-27 Fiscal Year with Authorization for Principals to Waive Fees in Case of Hardship Motion to approve the revised extracurricular activity fee schedule for the 2026-27 fiscal year with authorization for principals to waive fees in case of hardship, as submitted. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion passed 5-0 5.14 Minutes of Tucson Unified School District Governing Board Meeting – June 16, 2026 Motion to approve the minutes of the Governing Board Meeting held on June 16, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.15 Salary and Expense Vouchers - June 2026 Ratification of Salary and Expense Vouchers for the period beginning June 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah
Motion Passed 5-0 5.16 Student Activities Funds through June 30, 2026 Motion to approve the Summary of Student Activities Funds for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.17 Extracurricular Tax Credit Activity Programs Report by School Site through June 30, 2026 6:45 p.m. Motion to approve the Summary of Extracurricular Tax Credit Activity Balances for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.18 FY 2025-2026 Public Gifts and Donations to Schools Quarterly Report (4 th Quarter) Motion to approve the FY 2025-2026 Public Gifts and Donations to schools 4 th quarter report. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 5.19 FY 2025-2026 Governing Board Member Expenses Quarterly Report (4 th Quarter) Motion to accept the quarterly report on expenses incurred on behalf of individual Governing Board Members from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 5.2 through 5.19. Sadie Shaw requested item 5.9 and Val Romero requested item 5.17 for discussion. Resolution: Consent agenda items 5.2-5.19 were approved.
Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6. PUBLIC HEARING 6.1 Truth-in-Taxation Public Hearing: Adjacent Ways Property Tax Levy 7:06 p.m. 7. ACTION 7.1 FY2026-2027 Approval of Adjacent Ways Tax Levy 7:15 p.m. Motion to approve, by roll call vote, the Adjacent Ways property tax levy of $2.5 million and corresponding tax rate of $0.0543 for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 8. PUBLIC HEARING 8.1 Public Hearing for the FY2026-2027 Tucson Unified School District Annual Expenditure Budget 7:15 p.m. 7:25 p.m. 9. ACTION ITEM(S) 9.1 Adoption of the FY2026-2027 Tucson Unified School District Annual Expenditure Budget 7:29 p.m. Motion to adopt the annual expenditure budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year for the Tucson Unified School District, as presented. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah No: Sadie Shaw Motion passed 4-1
9.2 9.3 Administrative Appointments, Reassignments, and Transfers – Interim Assistant Principal, Pueblo High School 6:35 p.m. Motion to approve the selected candidate to serve as Interim Assistant Principal of Pueblo High School. Dr. Trujillo recommended Joy Smith to serve as the Interim Assistant Principal of Pueblo High School for the 2026-2027 School Year. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah : Motion Passed 5-0 Approval to Procure Goods and Services for Quarter 1 FY26-27 and Quarter 2 FY26-27 Bond Project Priorities 7:50 p.m. Motion to grant authority to the Purchasing Director, in conjunction with the Bond Program Manager, to procure goods and Services using approved TUSD and Cooperative Contracts for the next wave of bond projects, not to exceed +20% Contingency, where single purchases may exceed $250,000.00 for cumulative purchases with Cooperative Contract vendors in excess of $250,000.00. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5 – 0 9.4 Governing Board Policy EIA Property Insurance (Revision) – SECOND READING 7:59 p.m. Motion to approve the attached proposed revisions to Policy EIA Property Insurance. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 10. STUDY/INFORMATION ITEM(S) 10.1 TUSD Enrollment Stabilization Campaign - SY26-27 and Beyond 8:02 p.m. 11. FUTURE MEETING DATES and AGENDA ITEM(S) 11.1 Future Meeting Dates and Agenda Item(s) 8:37 p.m. 12. ADJOURNMENT 12.1 Adjourn Meeting
8:38 p.m. Ravi Shah adjourned the meeting.

DECORUM : The public is encouraged to attend City Council meetings in person or electronically. All persons in attendance are asked to observe the rules of politeness, propriety, decorum, and good conduct. Disrupting the meeting may result in being asked to leave or being removed from the building. ACCESSIBILITY : The City is committed to making its public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special/reasonable accommodations, contact the City Manager’s Office at (480) 644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. SERVICIOS EN ESPAÑOL : Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al (480) 644-2767. PARTICIPATION : A person may request to speak on agenda items for Council action or during "Items from citizens present" by submitting a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting via the kiosks, QR codes, or with City staff help in the lobby. Only one request to speak per person per item may be submitted. For an agenda item for Council action, comments need to relate to such item, and unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers is not limited and each speaker is limited to three minutes (if numerous speakers, reductions in time or a spokesperson may be implemented). During "Items from citizens present," a person may speak on general issues within the Council's jurisdiction, Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on issues raised, and unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers is limited to three and each speaker is limited to three minutes. CONSENT AGENDA : All items listed on the agenda with an asterisk (*) are on the consent agenda and will be considered as a group by the City Council, without any separate discussion of these items, unless a Councilmember or citizen requests an item be removed from the consent agenda. To request removal of an item from the consent agenda, submit a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting [see Participation above]. NOTICE : Pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.02, notice is hereby given that the City Council will hold a meeting open to the public at the date and time above. If the agenda indicates, the City Council may vote to go into executive session which will not be open to the public [A.R.S. § 38-431.03]. Members of the City Council may appear at the meeting in person, telephonically, or electronically. Children are welcome at City Council meetings, but remember meetings are video recorded; by allowing your child to attend, you consent to your child being recorded [A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9)]. ¹ For Regular City Council meetings held at 20 E. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second-floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. The Council may move the meeting from the Council Chambers to the first-floor Study Session room if there are technical issues, to ensure the orderly conduct of business, or if there are safety concerns; subject to technical limitations, the meeting will be televised in the Council Chambers and will remain livestreamed online for the public to continue to attend and listen to the deliberations. Visit https://www.mesaaz.gov/government/city-council-meetings for additional meeting and participation information. DECORUM : The public is encouraged to attend City Council meetings in person or electronically. All persons in attendance are asked to observe the rules of politeness, propriety, decorum, and good conduct. Disrupting the meeting may result in being asked to leave or being removed from the building. ACCESSIBILITY : The City is committed to making its public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special/reasonable accommodations, contact the City Manager’s Office at (480) 644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. SERVICIOS EN ESPAÑOL : Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al (480) 644-2767. PARTICIPATION : A person may request to speak on agenda items for Council action or during "Items from citizens present" by submitting a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting via the kiosks, QR codes, or with City staff help in the lobby. Only one request to speak per person per item may be submitted. For an agenda item for Council action, comments need to relate to such item, and unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers is not limited and each speaker is limited to three minutes (if numerous speakers, reductions in time or a spokesperson may be implemented). During "Items from citizens present," a person may speak on general issues within the Council's jurisdiction, Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on issues raised, and unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers is limited to three and each speaker is limited to three minutes. CONSENT AGENDA : All items listed on the agenda with an asterisk (*) are on the consent agenda and will be considered as a group by the City Council, without any separate discussion of these items, unless a Councilmember or citizen requests an item be removed from the consent agenda. To request removal of an item from the consent agenda, submit a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting [see Participation above]. NOTICE : Pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.02, notice is hereby given that the City Council will hold a meeting open to the public at the date and time above. If the agenda indicates, the City Council may vote to go into executive session which will not be open to the public [A.R.S. § 38-431.03]. Members of the City Council may appear at the meeting in person, telephonically, or electronically. Children are welcome at City Council meetings, but remember meetings are video recorded; by allowing your child to attend, you consent to your child being recorded [A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9)]. ¹ For Regular City Council meetings held at 20 E. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second-floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. The Council may move the meeting from the Council Chambers to the first-floor Study Session room if there are technical issues, to ensure the orderly conduct of business, or if there are safety concerns; subject to technical limitations, the meeting will be televised in the Council Chambers and will remain livestreamed online for the public to continue to attend and listen to the deliberations. Visit https://www.mesaaz.gov/government/city-council-meetings for additional meeting and participation information. DECORUM : The public is encouraged to attend City Council meetings in person or electronically. All persons attending the meeting are asked to observe the rules of politeness, propriety, decorum, and good conduct. Disrupting the meeting may result in being asked to leave or being removed from the building. ACCESSIBILITY : The City is committed to making its public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special/reasonable accommodations please contact the City Manager’s Office at (480) 644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. SERVICIOS EN ESPAÑOL : Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al (480) 644-2767. PARTICIPATION : Members of the public may address the City Council on a specific agenda item or during “Items from Citizens Present.” To speak in person, submit a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting using the kiosks in the lobby or through the City Clerk’s webpage (scan the QR code posted in the lobby). Only one request per person, per item, may be submitted. When called, please come to the lectern and state your name and district for the record. Comments on agenda items should relate to the item under consideration. During “Items from Citizens Present,” up to three speakers may address general issues within the City Council’s jurisdiction; Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on matters raised by speakers that are not listed on the agenda. Comments are generally limited to three minutes unless otherwise determined by the Mayor. If you are with a group, please designate a spokesperson. CONSENT AGENDA : All items listed on the agenda with an asterisk (*) are on the consent agenda which means they will be considered by the City Council as a group, without any separate discussion of these items, unless a Councilmember or citizen requests the item be removed from the consent agenda to be considered separately. To request removal of an item from the consent agenda, please submit a request to speak to the City Clerk prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting. NOTICE : Pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.02, notice is hereby given that the City Council will hold a meeting open to the public at the date and time above. If the agenda indicates, the City Council may vote to go into executive session which will not be open to the public [A.R.S. § 38-431.03]. Members of the City Council may appear at the meeting in person, telephonically, or electronically. Children are welcome at City Council meetings, but please remember meetings are video recorded; by allowing your child to attend, you consent to your child being recorded [A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9)]. ¹ For Regular City Council meetings held at 20 E. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. The Council may move the meeting from the Council Chambers to the first-floor Study Session room if there are technical issues, to ensure the orderly conduct of business, or if there are safety concerns; subject to technical limitations, the meeting will be televised in the Council Chambers and will remain livestreamed online for the public to continue to attend and listen to the deliberations. Visit https://www.mesaaz.gov/government/city-council-meetings for additional meeting and participation information. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second-floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. documents.text: City Council Meetings Agendas Approved Minutes Record of Comments (PDF, 140KB) Effective July 9, 2026: City Hall’s meeting guidelines have been updated to support safe, accessible and orderly public meetings. Signs ARE NOT permitted inside City Hall or during public meetings held at City Hall. Meeting Accessibility We are committed to making public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special accommodations, please contact the City Manager’s Office at 480-644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al 480-644-2767 . Schedule & Location Study Session Thursdays 7:30 a.m. City Hall (lower level) 20 E. Main St. Study Session (prior to Council Meeting) Generally first and third Monday of the month * 4:30 p.m. City Hall (lower level) 20 E. Main St. Council Meetings Generally first and third Monday of the month * 5:45 p.m. City Hall (upper level) 20 E. Main St. *Council meeting locations, days and times may change. Please check the calendar or agenda for the correct meeting information. Attending a Council Meeting We believe that providing access for citizens to communicate with the Council is vital for a strong representative local government. All council meetings are open to the public to attend in-person or electronically by watching live on local cable Mesa 11, YouTube and Facebook . The Mayor conducts Council meetings to accomplish the public’s business in a fair, efficient and orderly manner. Participating in a Council Meeting Members of the public may share comments with the Council in the following ways: Request to Speak at a Regular Council Meeting A person may request to speak on agenda items for Council action or during “Items from citizens present”. To do so, submit a request-to-speak form prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting using one of the digital kiosks available in the City Hall lobby. The form may also be accessed on a mobile device by scanning QR codes located throughout the lobby. Help is available for individuals in need of assistance with the digital system. The request to speak form becomes available at 5:00 p.m. on City Council meeting nights and must be completed prior to the scheduled start of the meeting. Each speaker must be present and is limited to three minutes, unless otherwise determined by the Mayor. Groups with similar comments are encouraged to designate a spokesperson. For agenda items for Council action , comments need to relate to such item and, unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers is not limited; however, if numerous participants request to speak on an agenda item for Council action, reductions in speaking time may be implemented or a spokesperson may be required. For “Items from Citizens Present,” a participant may speak on general issues within the Council’s jurisdiction, Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on issues raised, and, unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers is limited to three. Effective June 1, 2026: To ensure a fair and equitable process, speakers for "Items from Citizens Present" are selected at random from all requests submitted before the scheduled start time of the meeting. Selected speakers will be announced at the beginning of the meeting. This provides equitable access for residents and removes advantages based on sign-up timing. Watch a video about this process Submit Written Comments Residents who do not wish to speak at a meeting, but would like to share a comment or opinion for Council consideration may do so as follows: Submit an online comment card . Submit a paper comment card to City Clerk staff at the meeting location prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting. While the online comment card option is always available, if you want your online comment provided to the Councilmembers prior to the City Council meeting, it must be submitted prior to 2:00 p.m. on the day of the City Council meeting. Online comments submitted prior to 2:00 p.m. on the day of a City Council meeting will also be posted publicly on this page before the scheduled start time of the meeting. Online comments received after 2:00 p.m. and paper comments submitted to City Clerk staff at the meeting location prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting will be shared with the Councilmembers and posted publicly on this page the day after the City Council meeting . Please note, paper comments submitted to City Clerk staff at the meeting location prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting will not be provided to the Councilmembers at or prior to the meeting and will not be read aloud at the meeting (but will be sent to the Councilmembers and posted on this page the following day, as stated above). If you do not wish for your comments to be published on our website, you may email the Council directly as noted below. Email the Council Written feedback to the Council regarding agenda items or general issues may be sent to council@mesaaz.gov . Emails are not published on this page. Limited-Bag Policy and Security Screening To help ensure safe and efficient entry during City Council meetings at City Hall, a limited-bag policy is in place. Allowed Clear plastic, vinyl, or PVC bags up to 12” × 6” × 12” Small clutches or bags approximately the size of a folded 8.5” × 11” sheet (maximum 8.5” × 5.5”) Not Allowed Backpacks, large purses or totes, laptop or camera bags, and other non-clear bags exceeding 8.5” × 5.5” Notes and Exceptions Mesa does not use X-ray screening machines; bag limits and clear bag requirements help reduce manual searches and keep entry lines moving efficiently Medically necessary items, infant/diaper supplies, and assistive devices are permitted and may be subject to visual inspection No on-site bag storage is available; attendees should plan accordingly This policy applies to all City Council meetings at City Hall and may be adjusted based on attendance and safety needs Meeting Guidelines and Expectations Effective July 9, 2026: Signs ARE NOT permitted inside City Hall or during public meetings held at City Hall. All persons attending Council meetings are expected to observe rules of politeness, propriety and good conduct. Applause and audience commentary are not permitted. Individuals who disrupt the meeting may be asked to leave, removed and/or not permitted to return. To help ensure a safe and respectful environment for all attendees, the following guidelines apply: Signs and Presentation Materials To help maintain a safe, accessible and orderly meeting environment for everyone, signs, flags, banners, posters, placards and other held or carried display materials ARE NOT permitted inside City Hall or during public meetings. Individuals speaking on an agendized item may use presentation materials. Materials must be submitted to the City Clerk's Office (20 E. Main Street) at least one business day before the meeting. Materials will be provided during the speaker’s comment and returned after the meeting. Attire Visitors must wear basic attire, including a top, bottom and footwear (e.g., shirt, blouse, pants, shorts, skirt, shoes). Restricted Activities Protesting, petitioning, solicitation and leafletting are not permitted inside City Hall or in areas near entrances and parking lots. These areas must remain clear to ensure safe and unobstructed access for all visitors. City Hall and Facilities Use Policy (PDF, 710KB) Study Sessions All study sessions are open to the public to attend in-person, telephonically by calling 888-788-0099 or 877-853-5247 (toll free) using meeting ID 825 0808 5605, or electronically by watching live on local cable Mesa 11, YouTube and Facebook . Agendas & Minutes As part of each meeting, action may be taken on each agendized item, including zoning matters, awarding of contracts to purchase equipment, supplies or for construction improvements within the City, liquor license applications, ordinances, and resolutions. View Agendas Minutes of past City Council meetings are posted after they are approved by the City Council. The preliminary agenda of the next council meeting is posted approximately one week prior to meeting, and the final agenda, which incorporates any last minute changes to the preliminary agenda, is posted at least 24 hours prior to the meeting. View Minutes For copies of Council Minutes that are not listed, call the City Clerk's Office 480-644-2381 . Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 14, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/13/2026

HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/29/2026

Pima County AMENDED Meeting Agenda Board of Supervisors MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 1:10 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 1:30 PM Tuesday, August 11, 2026 Study Session PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC COMMENTS Written comments to the Board of Supervisors regarding the agenda items can be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov. All comments will be provided to the Board of Supervisors. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 8/6/2026

All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, August 25, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 8/26/2026
August 25, 2026 Board of Supervisors Meeting Agenda Clerk's Note: Members of the Pima County Board of Supervisors will attend either in person or by telephone, video or internet conferencing. The meeting can be streamed via the following links: BOS Agenda August 25, 2026 (http://pima.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=3), on YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/c/PimaCountyArizona/), or via Cox Cable Channel 96. CALL TO THE PUBLIC Individuals wishing to participate telephonically at Call to the Public must contact the Clerk of the Board’s Office at 520-724-8449, to register their request and obtain remote access information, by the deadline of Monday, August 24, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Call to the Public shall be scheduled for one hour each meeting unless extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. Speakers shall have up to three minutes to speak. However, for any meeting where 20 or more individuals have submitted speaker cards, each speaker's time shall be limited to two minutes. Please be aware that you may not be called upon to speak if the time for Call to the Public expires and is not extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. eComments can also be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, August 25, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 8/19/2026
August 25, 2026 Board of Supervisors Meeting Agenda Clerk's Note: Members of the Pima County Board of Supervisors will attend either in person or by telephone, video or internet conferencing. The meeting can be streamed via the following links: BOS Agenda August 25, 2026 (http://pima.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=3), on YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/c/PimaCountyArizona/), or via Cox Cable Channel 96. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT To be offered by Robert Ojeda, CEO, Pima Council on Aging. 4. CURRENT EVENTS/PUBLIC ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS 5. AGENDA ADJUSTMENTS 6. CALL TO THE PUBLIC Individuals wishing to participate telephonically at Call to the Public must contact the Clerk of the Board’s Office at 520-724-8449, to register their request and obtain remote access information, by the deadline of Monday, August 24, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Call to the Public shall be scheduled for one hour each meeting unless extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. Speakers shall have up to three minutes to speak. However, for any meeting where 20 or more individuals have submitted speaker cards, each speaker's time shall be limited to two minutes. Please be aware that you may not be called upon to speak if the time for Call to the Public expires and is not extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. eComments can also be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov. EXECUTIVE SESSION (Clerk's Note: As of the posting date of 8/19/26, no executive session item has been placed on the regular agenda. However, this is subject to any addendum. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 9/1/2026

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 22, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 9/23/2026

documents.text: Tucson Unified Governing Board Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Regular Meeting on Tuesday, October 6, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . ***REVISED 8/7/2026*** Governing Board Study Session Agenda August 10, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Pima Community College, District Office VIRTUAL MEETING* The Governing Board study session is live-streamed. Public members interested in following the proceedings virtually may visit the PCCTV YouTube homepage. To view the webinar, cut and paste the following link into your browser: https://www.youtube.com/c/PCCTVSTREAM. 1. REGULAR MEETING 1.1 Call To Order, Virtual Meeting* 2. ACTION (10 min.) 2.1 Intergovernmental Agreement: Arizona Department of Corrections for Educational Services Control#2695_Educational Services IGA (ASPC-Tucson)_Jun.2026 - Final.pdf The Chancellor recommends the Governing Board authorize the Chancellor or designee to execute a/an Amendment to Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) with the Arizona Department of Corrections, Rehabilitation and Reentry (ADCRR) for the purpose of delivering educational programs by the College’s Workforce Development Department to adult inmates at the Arizona State Prison Complex - Tucson for a three year term from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029 and authorize the Chancellor or designee to take any action or execute any other agreement necessary to accomplish the purposes of the agreement as may be limited by the Chancellor’s or designee previously authorized signature authority. 2.2 Experiential Education Intergovernmental Agreement: Arizona Board of Regents for and on behalf of Arizona State University and Pima County Community College District CN 2722--ASU-PCC Experiential Education Agreement (clean_8.5.26).pdf The Chancellor recommends the Governing Board authorize the Chancellor or designee to execute this Experiential Education IGA with the Arizona Board of Regents for and on behalf of ASU to benefit the College by providing ASU internships at the College’s food pantry and to further benefit students through practical, applied experience working at a social service organization. 2.3 Request to reschedule the September 14, 2026 board meeting to September 25, 2026 Recommend that the board approve the rescheduling of the September 14, 2026, board meeting to September 25, 2026.
3. DISCUSSION 3.1 Program Life Cycle The presentation and dialogue will focus on the process of developing new programs at the college, the program review process, and the options following program review, including program inactivation. Presented by: Dr. Ian Roark, Provost & Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs and Workforce Development Attachment: Program lifecycle presentation-August BOG study session (1).pdf 4. ADJOURNMENT 5. ANNOUNCEMENTS Option to recess into legal advice executive session - Pursuant to A.R.S. 38-431.03(A)(3) the Governing Board may vote to go into executive session for the purpose of obtaining legal advice from its legal counsel with respect to any item listed on this agenda or any addendum thereto; A.R.S. 38-431.03(A)(2) to discuss or consider records exempt by law from public inspection. The Governing Board reserves the right to take action on any agenda item. Please note that all individuals wishing to attend the Board meeting are subject to a search for security reasons. The public will have access to the board room thirty minutes before the scheduled meeting. To request a reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities, a minimum of 5 business days before the event is requested. Contact Phone: (520) 206-4539; Fax: (520) 206-4567. Members of the Governing Board may participate by telephone, video or internet conferencing. Meeting presentations will be posted within a reasonable time following the meeting.

Unapproved Page 1 of 4 Kearsarge Regional School Board 20 August 2026 Open to Public I. Call to Order Chair Mastin called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. II. Pledge of Allegiance The School Board led the pledge of allegiance. III. Roll Call Present : Art Bobruff, Nancy Glynn, Eric Gregoire, David Keith, Paul Lakevicius, Jamie MacKenna, Patrick McGowan, Alison Mastin, and Kristen Schultz. Absent : None Present : KREA representative Catharine Hyson IV. Public Hearing The Board held a public hearing regarding the appropriation of unanticipated funds. Chair Mastin read the following: As required per NH RSA 198:20-b, III, Kearsarge Regional School Board will conduct a public hearing to accept unanticipated funds from the New Hampshire Lead Remediation in Schools Drinking Water and Trust Fund Grant in the amount of $75,000. By accepting these funds, the District is required to perform and use the funds for lead remediation in drinking outlets testing at or above 5 parts per billion at the District’s schools. As advertised in the Concord Monitor of August 13, 2026. Ms. Schultz made a motion to accept and expend unanticipated New Hampshire Lead Remediation in Schools Drinking Water and Groundwater Trust Fund Grant revenue funds for the amount of $75,000. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). V. Approval of Minutes The Board reviewed the previously tabled minutes from the 23 July 2026 meeting. Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the minutes of 23 July 2026, as written. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 7-0-2 (Ms. Mastin & Mr. Keith abstained). The Board reviewed the minutes from the 6 August 2026 meeting. Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the minutes of 6 August 2026, as written. Ms. Schultz seconded. The motion carried 7-0-2 (Ms. Mastin & Mr. McGowan abstained). VI. Reports of Administration The following provided Administrative Reports: Chair Alison Mastin’s Report  She welcomed everyone to the new school year.  She noted that the Board is now full, having brought on Paul Lakevicius, a new Warner representative, over the summer. Superintendent Michael Bessette’s Report For a more comprehensive view, the Superintendent supplies the Board with a detailed Report to the Board ahead of each meeting, available online to the public. The following were touched on during the meeting:  He and Facilities Director Brett Paré attended Warner Zoning Board meeting regarding the results of a variance application, but are awaiting the results, which were tabled.  The Facilities Critical Needs Review process is at the pricing phase.  He commended Mr. Paré for his work on the Facilities Restructuring.  School readiness is on track.  However, he is concerned about several vacancies for substantive positions, including three of the four Associate Director positions.
Unapproved Page 2 of 4  Special Education may require a restructuring, and this is in the works currently. This may require the use of contracted services.  During his report, Ms. Glynn inquired about resources for her to engage as fully as possible as the newly appointed Chair of the Communications Committee and offered to help in any way possible. That information will be forthcoming. Business Administrator Larry LeBoeuf’s Report  None KREA Representative Catharine Hyson’s Report  None (school has not yet begun) Student Representative Cooper Russell’s Report  None (school has not yet begun) Actions taken by the Board: Mr. MacKenna made a motion to approve the review timeline from Superintendent Bessette’s Report to the Board and add it to the website under the Comprehensive Facilities Review. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). VI. Public Comment  Mag Francis of New London : She asked that the Board consider the fact that the discrepancy in numbers has to do with the fact that former Superintendent Fortney would include the numbers in Pre-K, whereas Mr. MacKenna’s data only encompasses K-12. She noted that the NESDEC model is not specific to Kearsarge. She was under the impression that this was going to be unique to the District, but it is a more generic model, which is not ultimately that useful. She also wanted to know if Lavallee Brensinger did something over the past year that was outside the original contract. And finally, she noted that the need to constantly do transfers is a sign of flawed budgeting processes, and asked that they try to fix this going forward. Ms. Schultz made a motion to exit public comment. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). VII. New Business A. Purchase Recommendation- Facilities Director Brett Paré 1. LaVallee Brensinger: This is for a contract extension with LaVallee Brensinger for $110,000. Mr. Paré clarified that the architecture firm attended all the school tours, Facilities B meetings, and were otherwise very heavily involved over the course of the last year. This would require two transfers to cover the cost. In light of the above public comment about transferring funds frequently for large-ticket items, the Board discussed at length what would happen if they did not extend the contract This could include having to start over from scratch with another firm, which would wipe out last year’s entire body of work. . Mr. MacKenna said he believes their extra services were well worth the cost. Ms. Mastin likewise noted that they have previously discussed this pending contract extension as far back as the spring, so it is not a spontaneous purchase. B. Purchase Recommendations- KRHS Principal Charlles Langille 1. FIRST Education Resources-Sole Source-$15,000: Tabled C. Purchase Recommendations- Student Services Director Larry Elliott 1. Staffing Mr. Elliott needs funding for the following staffing and contracted services: Educational Behavioral Consulting (BCBA/RBT): $275,000 Stepping Stones Group (OT): $135,000
Unapproved Page 3 of 4 Boothby Services (ACC, Medicaid, OT, (2) SLP, Teacher of Deaf): $300,000 LindaMood Bell: $34,000 SERESC (Contracted Services): $60,000 Enome-Goalbook: $14,875 EdLaw New England: $68,000 Terra Geer Consulting: $12,000 2. Transfers for Contracted Services: To cover the above costs, he needs to transfer $300,000 into Special Education Contracted Services from Special Education Salaries. D. Transfers & Encumbrances - Business Administrator Larry LeBoeuf 1. Transfers for $5K or less : Every year the Board is presented with any amounts less than $5,000 that need to be transferred. The total for the slate is $101,132.00. 2. Encumbrances : The district has more than $2,011,380.23 in still-open contracts that need to be encumbered from fiscal year 2025-2026 to 2026- 2027. 3. DOE 25/ MS 25 -Board Signature Mr. McGowan was absent at the last meeting and is the only Board member who still needs to sign this document. 4. Fund Balance Approval At the end of every school year, the Board has the authority to retain up to 5% of the budget. Mr. LeBoeuf is recommending 3%, which would amount to $1,410.486, giving $3,347.507 back to the taxpayers. Ms. Schultz recommended that they consider raising it to 5%, but Superintendent Bessette noted that these funds are not easily accessible and could cause a noticeable tax increase. Mr. McGowan said he thinks it’s worth exploring in the next cycle. 5. Bottinger Scholarship-$14,716.44 He needed a motion to deposit $14,716.44 into the Bottinger Scholarship Fund. Actions taken by the board: Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the contract extension with LaVallee Brensinger. Mr. Gregoire seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. McGowan made a motion to transfer $55,000 from two instructional lines to Capital Improvements/Architecture lines, totaling $110,000 to cover the above purchase recommendation. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the slate of contracted and staffing services, as presented. Mr. Gregoire seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to approve the transfer of $300,000 to cover the above slate of contracted services. Ms. Schultz seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the slate of transfers valued at less than $5,000. Mr. McGowan seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. Keith made a motion to approve the slate of encumbrances, as presented. Mr. McGowan seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to allow the Business Administrator to retain 3% of the budget.’ Ms. Glynn seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Dr. Bobruff made a motion to deposit the fund into the scholarship fund, as presented. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained).
Unapproved Page 4 of 4 VIII. Old Business A. Facilities Discussion on Potential Petition Plan for Closure: Superintendent Bessette asked that this be kept on the agenda from meeting to meeting to keep this possibility on the Board’s radar because the budgeting process may overshadow it in the month of September and he doesn’t want it to get lost in the shuffle. Mr. MacKenna recommended having an extra meeting scheduled for September 3, 2026, to give more time to tend to this matter. The Board discussed at length the decision- making process. Ms. Schultz noted she thinks a consolidation to one elementary school with 5 th graders at the middle school is the most efficient way to provide a quality education. Mr. MacKenna asked that Superintendent Bessette have a poster-sized visual for presentation purposes. B. Strategic Plan 2031: Nothing to report at this time other than the Superintendent hopes that the public is noticing its implementation. A summary overview will be provided to the public to inform them of the process. IX. Non-Public Ms. Schultz made a motion to go into non-public under RSA3: II (c) for reputation. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained).  The Board discussed out-of-district student placements. Mr. MacKenna made a motion to exit non-public session. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). X. Adjournment Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the slate of district placements, as presented in non-public. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to seal the non-public minutes for a period of 30 years. Mr. McGowan seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to adjourn. Ms. Schultz seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). The meeting adjourned at 8:31 p.m. Respectfully submitted, Amy Monroe, KRSD Notetaker

OPENING STATEMENT - NOTICE OF MEETING “Adequate notice of this meeting was advertised in the Daily Record and The Citizen on January 9, 2026 . In addition, it was mailed to the municipal offices at Denville Township, Rockaway Borough, Rockaway Township, and Wharton Borough for posting; mailed to the Morris County Clerk's Office; posted in the lobbies of Morris Hills and Morris Knolls High School, and the Board of Education building on January 6, 2026.” IV. Approval to accept the minutes: June 15, 2026 and July 20, 2026 Motion By: Seconded By: Roll Call Mr. Bertram Mrs. D’Asti Mr. Francia Ms. Levy Mr. Maher Mr. Napolitano Mr. Sera fi n Mrs. Yeager Mr. Wieczerzak AYES: NAYS: ABSTAIN: V. CHIEF SCHOOL ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT & CORRESPONDENCE VI. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES’ REPORTS VII. PUBLIC COMMENT STATEMENT “Please know that the Board of Education recognizes and respects your right to make public comments under Federal and State law, as well as Board Bylaw 0167. This is not a dialogue between the commenter and the Board. This is an opportunity for the Board to hear comments from the community. Questions regarding District operations or procedures should be directed to the appropriate administrative staff. Consistent with the Bylaw, public comment is limited to fi ve minutes. The board may interrupt, warn, or terminate public comment when the statement is too lengthy, abusive, obscene, or irrelevant. Further, the Board may request anyone to leave its meeting if that person does not observe reasonable decorum. Again, we respect your right to public comment, but please be aware of this caution and warning, the rights of other persons, and the Board’s rights concerning your comments.” VIII.
